Conflict: Material/Design and Circularity agents recommend polymer housings to maximize recycled content and recyclability, whereas Manufacture and In-Service agents recommend a recycled aluminum housing to prevent microplastic release and maximize durability.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Recycled aluminum alloy shell with mechanical rubber grips
Rationale: An aluminum shell provides superior durability and reliability against physical drops, preventing premature obsolescence under ESPR Annex I (a). Furthermore, avoiding overmolded polymers eliminates microplastic and nanoplastic release during both production and in-service wear under ESPR Annex I (p).

Conflict: Material, In-Service, and Circularity agents recommend threaded fasteners for ease of disassembly, whereas the Manufacture agent highlights that this increases assembly cycle times compared to ultrasonic welding or adhesives.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Threaded metal fasteners (Torx screws) into brass inserts
Rationale: Threaded fasteners allow non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly, which is a non-negotiable requirement for ease of repair, maintenance, upgrading, and refurbishment under ESPR Annex I (b) and (c), over-riding manufacturing cycle-time preferences.

Conflict: Circularity and Material agents recommend a brushless DC motor with mechanically secured magnets, whereas the Manufacture agent recommends a brushed DC motor to simplify production and reduce initial material footprint.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with mechanically secured, easily extractable permanent magnets
Rationale: A BLDC motor drastically increases technical lifetime and energy efficiency in use under ESPR Annex I (a) and (g). Mechanically securing the magnets instead of gluing them ensures they can be easily extracted at end-of-life, facilitating high-quality recycling and critical material recovery under ESPR Annex I (d).

Conflict: In-Service and Circularity agents recommend active fan cooling to prevent thermal degradation, whereas Material and Manufacture agents recommend purely passive cooling to simplify assembly and avoid additional components.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Passive cooling via open ventilation slots combined with a mechanical shaft-mounted fan (no potting compounds)
Rationale: This balanced approach ensures active cooling to protect the motor and battery from thermal degradation, improving durability under ESPR Annex I (a), while avoiding chemical potting compounds that act as substances of concern and hinder recycling under ESPR Annex I (e).

Conflict: Circularity, Material, and In-Service agents recommend a fully modular plug-and-play architecture, whereas the Manufacture agent recommends a monolithic integrated design to simplify the production line and reduce manufacturing waste.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Modular cartridge-based architecture with separate, pluggable modules
Rationale: A modular architecture ensures that individual faulty components can be easily replaced or upgraded, directly addressing ease of repair, maintenance, and upgrading under ESPR Annex I (b) and (c). Monolithic designs that prevent repair are non-compliant with these circularity mandates.

Conflict: In-Service, Material, and Circularity agents recommend a removable and standardized slide-on battery pack, whereas the Manufacture agent recommends a corded AC power supply to completely avoid battery manufacturing impacts.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Removable and standardized slide-on Li-ion battery pack with fastener-assembled cells
Rationale: A corded connection fails the core functional performance and conditions of use under ESPR Annex I (s) for a 'cordless screwdriver'. To maintain cordless utility while complying with repairability under ESPR Annex I (b) and safe EoL recycling, a removable, standardized, and fastener-assembled battery pack is selected.
